> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **13** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0951a00315a256cdb5ae09367f56a78b01636d6b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `da8c1c90b353ce87a487ffe195feeb2d33af19ec` — the merge of head `a1260e572f68a044e90b689eb0f360fd4f2813a3` into base `0951a00315a256cdb5ae09367f56a78b01636d6b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin da8c1c90b353ce87a487ffe195feeb2d33af19ec && git checkout da8c1c90b353ce87a487ffe195feeb2d33af19ec
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0951a00315a256cdb5ae09367f56a78b01636d6b a1260e572f68a044e90b689eb0f360fd4f2813a3 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0951a00315a256cdb5ae09367f56a78b01636d6b && git merge --no-ff a1260e572f68a044e90b689eb0f360fd4f2813a3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0951a00315a256cdb5ae09367f56a78b01636d6b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0951a00315a256cdb5ae09367f56a78b01636d6b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `a1260e572f68a044e90b689eb0f360fd4f2813a3`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #25549 (body, the director increment 6377536821, rulings 6377738234 / 6377844010 / 6378238137 and the retraction pair, the Claim 6378250869, the os-dev-report 6378915159), PR #25591 (body, 12-file list, net diff against `main`), and the check-runs on the head. Review face: declaration (`Clause-②: yes` on the PR body and the changeset; no published schema or governed path in the committed tree — `packages/spec` is untouched).

### ① Derived judgments

The ruling (letter A) admits exactly one new accept-set: on an effective-`public` object, a share or sharing rule whose recipient is a `user` who is an `external` member of the record's organization. Each change the diff implies, read against that:

1. **`inertGrantReason(object, recipient?)` — the object half is unchanged, the recipient half is bounded.** Right. The new arm fires only when `effectiveSharingModel(schema) === 'public'` AND `hasOwnerField(schema)` AND `!hasPhantomOwnerAnchor(schema)` AND a recipient standing was supplied. `public_read` (effective `read`) is not touched; owner-less objects, phantom-anchor federated objects, `controlled_by_parent` details and the bypass set keep their caller-free refusal for every recipient (the arms are tested in order; `controlled_by_parent` and bypass return before the public arm). With `recipient` omitted the arm refuses as before, so `assertNotInertGrant(object)` on its own is not widened.
2. **Recipient population test (`isExternalMemberIn`).** Right. One `sys_member` row with `user_id` = recipient and `organization_id` = the resolved organization, whose role list is exactly `external` (distinct, trimmed, lower-cased tokens, length 1). I compared it to plugin-auth's `isExternalMembershipRole` / `roleTokens` on `main` (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/external-membership.ts:48-62`): same tokenisation, same `MEMBERSHIP_ROLE_EXTERNAL` constant from `@objectstack/spec`. `external,member` is refused (pinned). A user external in org B and member of org A is refused on an org A record; the reverse user is admitted (pinned). Non-`user` recipient types never reach the new arm: `grant()` still refuses them `VALIDATION_FAILED` before any pre-flight.
3. **Where the recipient half runs.** Right, and narrower than it had to be. `assertRecipientNotInert` runs on both paths after the organization is resolved; on the direct path after `assertSharingEnforced` (existence) and `assertCanManageShares` (D1), so an unauthorised caller gets 403/404 and never learns a recipient's population. The granter is never an input (system caller and owner get the same two answers, pinned). `organizationId === null` yields `unknown-organization` and a named `SHARING_NOT_ENABLED` refusal — the acceptance item "both paths resolve the recipient's role in the object's organization, or refuse with a named reason" is met. The direct path's fallback to the session's organization applies only to a record that carries no organization at all (`reading.kind === 'none'`), not to a failed read; that is the pre-existing commit-3f64fe6c6 shape and is the only organization such a record has.
4. **Rule materialisation.** Right. `grantOrAbsorbOrganizationRefusal` returns a three-way outcome; only a refusal carrying the `INTERNAL_RECIPIENT_REFUSAL` symbol becomes `'internal'` (skipped, not counted as refused); every other `SHARING_NOT_ENABLED` still propagates and aborts the rule's pass (the `[#8207]` block now pins the four aborting classes and a new case pins that the public class mints nothing for an internal recipient). All three passes (`reconcile`, `reconcileForRecord`, `reconcileRuleForUser`) thread `skipped` into `withInternalHalfNote`, which writes one `note` on the pass result and one log line per pass. The acceptance item "one report line when the staff half is skipped" is met, and the PR measured the route that surfaces it (`POST /sharing/rules/:idOrName/evaluate` answers the result unfiltered).
5. **Internal-only invariants still hold.** Checked against the read side, which this diff does not touch: `buildReadFilter` returns `null` for an internal reader on a public object (`owdForPrincipal(...) !== 'private'` at `sharing-service.ts:612` on the head), so a share row minted for an external is never consulted for staff, and no row is minted for an internal recipient on either path (dogfood: 422, zero `sys_record_share` rows; unit: zero rows). For the external, the floored filter is `{$or: [{owner_id: me}, {id: {$in: [shared]}}]}` — exactly the record handed to it (pinned at the unit level and over REST on a showcase boot).
6. **Lint** `sharing-rule-object-not-shareable`: the public arm drops to `warning` with the ruled wording "effective for external recipients only"; the `controlled_by_parent` arm stays `error`. Right — item 3 of the ruling, and the lint's verdict function still mirrors the runtime's object half.
7. **Docs / examples / registry comment.** `sharing-rules.mdx` gains the ruled paragraph; `permissions/index.mdx`, `examples/app-crm/objectstack.config.ts` and the `AUTHORING_RULES` comment said the rule "fails the build" — a sentence this round makes false, corrected. Right (see ③ for the file-surface flag).
8. **Public surface.** No spec key, value or type changes (`Metadata-protocol: none` on the card); `SharingRuleReconcilePassResult.note?` is an optional field on plugin-sharing's own interface, not the spec's `SharingRuleEvaluationResult`; `isInternalRecipientRefusal` is a new named export of plugin-sharing. Additive, minor.

Adversarial probes that found nothing wider than the ruling: a `user` whose membership row is in another organization (refused); a role list with a second token (refused); a public object with no `owner_id` (refused for an external — pinned); a phantom-anchor federated public object (refused — guarded in the arm); a system caller (same answer as a user caller); an unauthorised caller (403 first); a `public_read` object (effective `read`, arm never reached); a `controlled_by_parent` detail (refused before the arm).

Two small wording-level observations, neither blocking:

- `system-caller-inert-grant.test.ts:196` says the public class is "pinned ... in `external-recipient-public-object.test.ts`"; no file of that name exists on the head (the pins live in the same file's new block 3). Stale comment, fix at leisure.
- When a rule-path grant resolves no organization (a deployment-wide rule over a record with no organization), the refusal is `unknown-organization`, still carries the `INTERNAL_RECIPIENT_REFUSAL` mark, and the pass counts it under the "internal recipients skipped" note. Fail-closed and no row is written, so the ruling is kept; the note's wording slightly misnames that case.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/25549-external-share-public-object.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-sharing` minor, `@objectstack/lint` minor. Matches what the diff publishes: a widened accept-set on `SharingService.grant`, a new optional result field and a new named export in plugin-sharing; a severity drop and new wording in lint. No major (nothing removed), not patch (behaviour admitted that was refused). The `Clause-②:` line reads `yes (widening: the grant door and the materialiser admit one recipient population on effective-public objects)` on both the PR body and the changeset, identically, and names the widening this diff makes and no other. `Metadata-protocol: semantic` on the changeset (the card body said `none`; the Claim said `semantic`, the dev reports `check-changeset-no-major` exit 0 and the `Check Changeset` check-run is green twice on the head) — consistent with a lint refusal becoming advice, and the two lines agree between PR body and changeset.

Check-runs on the head: every completed run is `success` or `skipped` (opt-in / conditional lanes). Completed green: Lint & Repo Gates, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check PR Size, Spec property liveness, Dogfood Regression Gate, Build Docs, all Lint lanes, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Check Documentation Links, the four PR-claim guards, Flag docs affected by code changes. Still `in_progress` when this record was rendered: Test Core 1/6–6/6, Build Core, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · workspace. The verdict below is judged on the completed runs and the diff; the dev's local runs (plugin-sharing 1233/1233, lint 7237/7237, dogfood file 13/13, 104/104 dispatch-gate families) are the dev's claim, not a gate verdict, and are not what carries it.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions: []`, `out_of_scope_findings: []`. The six `deviations` in the os-dev-report, each answered:

1. **File surface — three files outside the Claim's list** (`permissions/index.mdx`, `examples/app-crm/objectstack.config.ts`, `lint/src/authoring-rules.ts`). Accepted: each is a shipped sentence this change falsifies ("fails the build" / "build error"), the edits are comment- or prose-only, and none adds behaviour. Seat: add the three paths to the Claim's file surface as the dev asks.
2. **Changeset `minor`, `Metadata-protocol: semantic` where the card said `none`.** Accepted — see ②; the semantic line is what the gate reads and it is green.
3. **Unit test placed in `system-caller-inert-grant.test.ts`** rather than a new file. Accepted (reuses the pinned engine double; no ledger change). The stale cross-reference at line 196 noted in ① follows from this.
4. **`note` declared on plugin-sharing's `SharingRuleReconcilePassResult`, not on the spec's type.** Accepted; keeps `packages/spec` out of the diff and the tier at TIER_DEFAULT. If a client is ever to read the note from the typed evaluate result, that is a spec change for a later card.
5. **PR body erratum**: Acceptance note "Spec contract docblock" ends "with the ADR line below", and no ADR line is in the PR. Escalated to the seat with the dev's PATCH text: replace "with the ADR line below" by "with the ADR-0111 line drafted in the os-dev-report". Prose only; does not affect the verdict.
6. **ADR-0111 D7 dated line left out (Tier H)** — correct per the Claim (`⛔ no ADR edit`); the draft rides in `adr_0111_draft`. Escalated to the seat to route with the Tier H docs PR for #25233.

Further flag raised by the dev and not a deviation: `spec_docblock_followup` — `ISharingService.grant`'s docblock in `packages/spec/src/contracts/sharing-service.ts` still says a share on a public object "enforces nothing", now half true. Comment-only on a published d.ts, outside this claim's surface. Escalated to the seat to route alongside item 6.

PR-body acceptance notes read and agreed: the error-order change on a public object (D1 before the recipient half — deliberate, tested, narrower not wider); existing `source: 'rule'` rows for internal recipients on public objects minted by older builds are left standing and are never consulted for that population (no leak; a follow-up purge is optional hygiene).

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-eflr1z`
Reviewed-by: `session_013odhA26dvzy7pQmevdTTvy/contract-review-agent`

**VERDICT: PASS**

A `user` recipient who is exactly an `external` member of the record's organization may be shared a record of an effective-`public` object that has a real owner. Both paths do this: the grant door and the rule materialiser. `public_read`, owner-less, phantom-anchor, `controlled_by_parent` and bypass objects keep the caller-free refusal. Internal recipients get no rows on either path. An unresolved organization is refused with a named reason. The granter is never an input.
